description: Council to review 1st Avenue Bus Rapid Transit design options.
Concerns raised on accessibility, business access, project delays.
Integration with Downtown Event & Entertainment District questioned.

chips.text: Bus riders and businesses, including Capital Music Club, are affected.
Why transit signal priority, DED impacts, and new shelter designs were not considered.
Bus Riders of Saskatoon advocate for dedicated lanes and timely project completion.

description: Adaptive traffic signals adjust timings for better flow.
Pilot suggested for Circle Drive North corridor.
Costs $50,000 capital, $2,500 annually operating per intersection.

chips.text: Staff noted they would likely explore this technology in future due to AI advancements.
Adaptive signal control can decrease fuel consumption and vehicle emissions.
Administration will continue assessing adaptive signal control technology.

description: City to consider 48-hour grace for residential accessible parking tickets.
Not displaying a valid placard currently incurs a $210 fine.

chips.text: Homeowners with residential accessible parking stalls.
City does not track accessible parking tickets by residential area.
Resident Karen Kobussen requested a 48-hour grace period for tickets.
Administration will report back on policy amendment feasibility.

speakers.name: Karen Kobussen
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Request to Amend Council Policy On-Street Accessible Parking and Bylaw
said: Requested amending policy for residential accessible parking stalls.
Homeowners should get 48 hours to display forgotten placard.
Current policy is punitive; other jurisdictions allow grace period.
